title: CMake: Revert libgcrypt back to 1.11.2 on Windows
description:
This PR reverts part of 44b886ac28d739465afb858c6bf66d520a9ac64c. On my Windwos 11 24H2 (with SDK 10.0.26100.0), calling gcry_check_version(NULL) ~~segfaults~~ (edit: no actually) blows up during start. I've bisected the bug, and it seems to have happened between version 1.11.2 and version 1.12.0.

![image](/uploads/57a4238b2f2b4d7412437af81371306a/image.png){width=900 height=431}

This should be reported upstream, but [their bugtracker](https://dev.gnupg.org/) is down and mailing lists isn't my cup of tea. In the mean time let's rollback.

AI-Assisted: no

notes.body: libgcrypt 1.12.2 is a [security fix](https://lists.gnupg.org/pipermail/gnupg-announce/2026q2/000503.html). It might make sense to switch to 1.11.3 (which has the same fixes), assuming the crash was introduced in the 1.12 branch.

We repackage the MSYS2 [mingw-w64-clang-x86_64-libgcrypt](https://packages.msys2.org/packages/mingw-w64-clang-x86_64-libgcrypt) in this case. Unfortunately it doesn't look like they ship PDB files which might make it tricky to track down the issue.

> We repackage the MSYS2 [mingw-w64-clang-x86_64-libgcrypt](https://packages.msys2.org/packages/mingw-w64-clang-x86_64-libgcrypt) in this case.

Unfortunately, they [skipped over 1.11.3](https://github.com/msys2/MINGW-packages/commits/master/mingw-w64-libgcrypt), which means we need to update our packaging to build libgcrypt ourselves. I'll add that to my to-do list, and in the mean time approve this.

@gpotter2 - Curiosity question (because I've had this issue too) - Do you have a dev environment for multiple versions of Wireshark (i.e. master and 4.6 and/or 4.4)?  I haven't fully tested this, but I thought maybe the issue on my end was the "global" build variables (i.e. WIRESHARK_BASE_DIR and WIRESHARK_LIB_DIR) trying to support multiple dev environments concurrently.
I also only get this issue when running from Visual Studio.  Building an installer for Wireshark and running that, I don't have this issue...

@mmann78 I only build master with indeed global system wide variables.

I must say I was in a rush when I made this PR, my understanding of the issue is limited. But it's true that the nightly automated build from yesterday worked fine (I tested it to check my ETW PR), so it might be something that somehow only happens from within Visual Studio (?).
Also sorry I missed your thread in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/24714#note_3311944927 !

@mmann78 @gpotter2 I can't replicate the problem here, but I build and run Wireshark from a Windows Terminal cmd prompt instead of Visual Studio. If this is a case of a wrong DLL being loaded, I wonder if a modern dependency walker (Dependencies? WinDepends?) might reveal something.

OK, I *can* replicate it here if I run Wireshark under Visual Studio, but not from a command prompt. I compared the list of DLLs loaded by Wireshark.exe in both cases using Process Explorer, but nothing obvious jumped out.

> Without a PDB for libgcrypt, that makes it harder to track down. Google's AI seems to think that Microsoft offers a PDB for ntdll from its public symbol server, but from looking at some of the references it provides, it might have misread it.

It's correct, the public PDB of ntdll is provided, but I'm unsure it will help in this case as the issue seems to be happening before that.

If no one else is looking at the issue, I can try to recompile libgcrypt to have the pdb and be able to debug it by tomorrow :)

> (Off-topic, but it seems that this libgcrypt commit also introduces the creation of some kind of empty configuration folder that remains after Wireshark uninstallation

The extra directory was added to deal with a security issue that 1.11.3/1.12.x fixes, reading out of the `/etc/gcrypt` directory even on Windows (which could be created by any user.) 53f456891b42ad8151dd665b18295176e87e91ce

We might be able to check for the version of gcrypt and avoid creating the directory in that case.
Or just not create it as we are distributing a fixed version now.

> I think it's crashing because you're supposed to use `FreeLibrary` that [checks references](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/libloaderapi/nf-libloaderapi-freelibrary) unlike `CloseHandle` before freeing.

I'm not even sure it's valid to pass an `HMODULE` returned from `LoadLibraryEx()` to `CloseHandle()`; yes, the "H" in "HMODULE" may mean "handle", but I'm not sure they're the same *type* of "handle".

You might want to change the definition of `handle` from `void *handle` to `HMODULE handle`, given that `loadLibraryEx` is declared as returning an`HMODULE`. It may be that `HMODULE` and `HANDLE` are of type `void *` or something else, but that doesn't mean they should be treated as interchangeable.
The `LoadLibraryEx` / `FreeLibrary` issue has been fixed upstream: https://lists.gnupg.org/pipermail/gcrypt-devel/2026-May/006099.html.

This resulted in #21337. Calling `FreeLibrary` is correct, but it appears that the library is being loaded (thus `_gcry_get_sysconfdir()` is being called) every single time `gcry_md_write` is called in a loop, because there's a tremendous number of new `atexit()` calls that have to be from unloading the library (there's no `atexit` in the gcrypt source itself). That's not supposed to happen; everywhere that calls `_gcry_get_sysconfdir()` has static variables that are intended to make it only called once, and you can see the `appdata` static variable above, so the loop should not be entered on subsequent calls.
